question.problem: A particle $P$ of mass $3\,kg$ moves along the $x$-axis from rest at the origin with an acceleration of magnitude $3\sqrt{t}\,{m/s}^{2},$ where the acceleration acts in the direction of increasing $x,$ and $t\ge 0$ is the time in seconds. Calculate the particle's kinetic energy at time $t=1\,s.$
question.worked_solution:
The kinetic energy of a particle with mass $m$ and velocity $v$ is given by

$$
\text{KE}=\frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2}.
$$

When the mass and velocity are measured in kilograms and meters per second, respectively, the particle's kinetic energy is measured in Joules ($J$).

First, we find $v(t)$ by integrating the acceleration with respect to time:

$$
\begin{aligned}v(t) & =\int a(t)\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =\int 3\sqrt{t}\,\text{d}t \\ v(t) & =2{t}^{3/2}+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $v(0)=0.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
0=2({0}^{3/2})+C\,⟹\,C=0.
$$

Hence, the velocity of the particle at time $t$ is $v(t)=2{t}^{3/2}.$ In particular, its velocity at time $t=1\,s$ is

$$
v=v(1)=2({1}^{3/2})=2\,m/s.
$$

Therefore, the kinetic energy of the particle at $t=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{KE} & =\frac{1}{2}m{v}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 3\cdot {2}^{2} \\  & =6\,J.\end{aligned}
$$
